the development of within-network connectivity between late-childhood and adulthood is associated with the maturation of cognitive control abilities.

how the development of the human brain is associated with the maturation of cognitive and social behavior.
the developmental trajectory of brain networks and the relationship between network development and behavior.

there are both similarities and differences in the development of within- and between network connectivity between late childhood to adulthood.
the development of these networks occurred between the late childhood and adult age groups, and that these changes are associated with the development of cognitive control.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the development of the brain from late childhood to adulthood is a dynamic process in which the brain restructures and strengthens its connections in order to support mature cognitive control and self-directed behavior.
the maturation of these brain systems supports the emergence of adult-like cognitive control.
the maturation of these brain systems is associated with improved inhibitory control, social cognition, self-directed thought, and working memory.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the maturation of functional connectivity between late childhood (age 10-11) and adulthood (age 21-23) is not uniform across the brain, and instead, is regionally specific.
the maturation of the brain from late childhood through adolescence to adulthood involves changes in both connectivity within the TP and TN networks and between these two networks.
the development of these networks occurs in specific regions and not in a diffuse manner across the entire brain.
